messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: high error rate on inference-route-prod — 5xx spike over last 3m, page sent to oncall-sre. Link: https://redwood.incidents/1881234567
oncall-sre: ACK — looking. jumping into logs and metrics now. ETA 5
oncall-sre: quick note: customers seeing API 500/502 intermittently, latency also up to 1.8s p50 on text-gen
alice.m: I'm seeing a flood of `grpc: connection error` entries on the ingress ELB logs starting ~1881234500. forwarding snippet
alice.m: ```
2026-04-12T10:22:01Z ingress-1 pod-abc123 "GET /v1/generate 502" "grpc: connection error"
2026-04-12T10:22:02Z ingress-2 pod-def456 "POST /v1/chat 502" "upstream read: connection reset by peer"
```
ben_p: I can run a quick grep across the pathfinder logs, do we have any sampling or forwarder changes in the last deploy window?
carmen_ops: I rolled out a logging-sampling change at 10:15 UTC to reduce noise (reduced to 5% for debug logs) — shouldn't affect 5xx counters but noting it here.
eva_reliability: tagging: possible correlation: our network egress quota bumped at 10:20 for the cluster, but that was a control-plane op, not infra change to pods
oncall-sre: hypothesis 1: upstream model-worker pods are hitting resource exhaustion (OOM/restart) causing connection resets. hypothesis 2: log-forwarder sampling change inadvertently toggled sidecar buffering and caused TCP resets.
oncall-sre: running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime` now
alice.m: watching pod restarts: workers in inference-pool-3 show 1-2 restarts around 10:21-10:23
ben_p: can someone run a quick ad-hoc query in elsa to fetch tail of model-worker logs for that time range? I don't have access to the prod indices for pathfinder
alice.m: shared query: `index:model-worker* | where timestamp >= 2026-04-12T10:18:00Z and timestamp <= 2026-04-12T10:26:00Z | parse "error=*" as err | top err by count` — results: heavy `kafka: conn reset` and `kvcache: shard timeout`
carmen_ops: kafka conn reset is weird — we didn't touch kafka
oncall-sre: mitigation attempt 1: scaled inference-pool-3 from 12 -> 18 replicas (kubectl scale deployment inference-pool-3 --replicas=18). watching for decreased 5xx
deploy-bot: deploy event: scaled inference-pool-3 by oncall-sre (manual). timestamp=1881234670
oncall-sre: after scale, 5xx rate dropped ~40% in the next 90s but did not return to baseline
eva_reliability: digging into network metrics — pod egress errors spiked at 10:20, matching ingress errors. Could be a transient networking fabric flake in the region.
alice.m: but traces show many requests failing during the model-call stage, and the trace IDs are missing in traces backend for that window — looks like we lost spans
ben_p: that's probably the sampling/frontier issue — Carmen, you said you changed sampling to 5%. Did the change touch trace/span sampling as well or only debug logs?
carmen_ops: only debug logs. I did not touch trace sampling. But I also rotated the forwarder config at 10:17 to change buffer settings (small tweak). I can revert that immediately if we want.
oncall-sre: mitigation attempt 2: revert forwarder buffer change to previous config (applied). monitoring... 
alice.m: after revert, log ingestion rate for model-worker indices increased back to expected levels (partial recovery)
eva_reliability: dashboards: p50 latency back to ~350ms, p95 ~820ms, errors down to near baseline but a few outliers remain
oncall-sre: customer impact: per billing-routes, ~0.6% of requests experienced 5xx between 10:20–10:26. Major customers affected: two enterprise tenants saw retry storms reported.
oncall-sre: created an incident timeline document (internal): https://redwood.incidents/timeline/1881234567 (will attach logs and queries)
ben_p: for RCA we need: full pod restart timeline, forwarder config diff, trace sampling settings, and any control-plane throttles. I'll collect pod restarts and forwarder diffs now.
alice.m: attaching quick `kubectl describe pod` excerpts in thread:
```
Name: pod-abc123
Restart Count: 2
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age    From               Message
  ----    ------     ----   ----               -------
  Warning Back-off   6m     kubelet, node-5     Back-off restarting failed container
```
eva_reliability: recorded that a monitoring alert for network egress throttle hit 10:19:58 but was resolved by control-plane 10:21:00
carmen_ops: I also pulled the forwarder config diff: I changed `buffer.max_bytes`  from 8mb -> 512kb and `flush.interval_ms` 1000 -> 300. Rolling back restores previous values. I can open a PR to add a canary before changing in prod.
oncall-sre: action items for postmortem (assigned):
- ben_p: collect pod restart + node metrics (node cpu/ram/conn) — assigned
- carmen_ops: forwarder config diff + timeline + PR for safer rollout — assigned
- alice.m: save log excerpt bundle and query results to incident s3 — assigned
- eva_reliability: correlate network fabric events and control-plane ops — assigned
oncall-sre: before we close P0, we need to verify no latent damage to KV cache and run a small canary load for 15m
alice.m: canary run started at 10:40, 15m steady, no errors observed, will report in 10:55
ben_p: one outstanding question: why did the buffer change correlate with `kafka: conn reset` and `kvcache: shard timeout`? hypothesis: reduced buffer led to increased connection churn upstream to kafka, exposing a timing bug in the worker
carmen_ops: agreed. I will include that hypothesis in the RCA draft and note that the sampling change was not in traces but buffer config had side effects.
oncall-sre: thank you team, transitioning to post-incident mode. leaving channel open for RCA comments.
alice.m: noted — I'll attach the final log bundle and a short customer impact blurb for CS
deploy-bot: rollback note: forwarder config reverted by carmen_ops (timestamp=1881234762)
incidents-bot: Incident P0 resolved: error rate returned to baseline, mitigation steps applied, RCA in progress. Link: https://redwood.incidents/1881234567/summary :white_check_mark:
